We have template 1914386. Need to propose retrosynthesis route for target SMILES: COC(C1(C=C1[Si](C)(C)C)/C=C/C2=CC=CC=C2)=O.

We need to apply this template in retrosynthetic direction (i.e., break target into precursors). The template's retro_smarts: '[C;D1;H3:9]-[#14:10](-[C;D1;H3:11])(-[C;D1;H3:12])-[C;H0;D3;+0:13]1=[CH;D2;+0:14]-[C;H0;D4;+0:1]-1(/[CH;D2;+0:2]=[CH;D2;+0:3]/[c:4])-[C:5](=[O;D1;H0:6])-[#8:7]-[C;D1;H3:8]>>O=[C;H0;D3;+0:1](-[CH2;D2;+0:2]-[CH2;D2;+0:3]-[c:4])-[C:5](=[O;D1;H0:6])-[#8:7]-[C;D1;H3:8].[C;D1;H3:9]-[#14:10](-[C;D1;H3:11])(-[C;D1;H3:12])-[C;H0;D2;+0:13]#[CH;D1;+0:14]'

So forward reaction (template) transforms two fragments: a silyl alkyne? Actually product side is two fragments: an ester (maybe) and a silyl alkyne. The retro direction (apply to target) will split target into those two fragments.

Our target: COC(C1(C=C1[Si](C)(C)C)/C=C/C2=CC=CC=C2)=O

Let's parse: It's a methyl ester (COC(=O) ...). Actually "COC(...)=O" is methyl ester of something: OCH3 attached to carbonyl carbon. The carbonyl carbon attached to C1(...). So target is methyl ester of a phenyl-substituted cyclobutene? Wait.

SMILES: C O C ( C1( C= C1 [Si](C)(C)C ) /C=C/ C2=CC=CC=C2 ) = O

So carbonyl carbon attached to OCH3 and to C1(...). C1 is a cyclobutene? C1(C=C1[Si](C)(C)C) is a cyclobutene with a silyl substituent on one double bond carbon? Actually C1(C=C1[Si](C)(C)C) is a cyclobutene where carbon 1 is sp3 attached to carbonyl carbon, and also double bond to C=C1? Might be a cyclobutene ring fused? Hard.

But template expects product containing a silyl alkyne fragment attached to carbonyl? Wait product side: O=[C;H0;D3;+0:1](-[CH2;D2;+0:2]-[CH2;D2;+0:3]-[c:4])-[C:5](=[O;D1;H0:6])-[#8:7]-[C;D1;H3:8] . That's an ester with a phenylpropyl chain? Actually O=C( -CH2-CH2-aryl ) -C(=O)-O-CH3? Wait.

Let's decode: O=[C:1](-[CH2:2]-[CH2:3]-[c:4])-[C:5](=[O:6])-[#8:7]-[C:8] . This looks like a carbonyl (acid) attached to CH2CH2-aryl, then attached to C(=O)O-CH3? Actually O=[C](-CH2-CH2-aryl)-C(=O)-O-CH3. That's methyl ester of phenylpropionic acid? Yes.

Second fragment: [C;D1;H3:9]-[#14:10](-[C;D1;H3:11])(-[C;D1;H3:12])-[C;H0;D2;+0:13]#[CH;D1;+0:14] . That's a silyl-substituted alkyne: R- Si(CH3)3 attached to carbon of alkyne? Actually carbon 13 is sp2? It's a carbon attached to Si and triple bond to CH. So it's a silyl alkyne.

Thus retrosynthesis: target splits into methyl ester of phenylpropionic acid (or similar) and a silyl alkyne.

Our target appears to be a silyl-substituted cyclobutene attached to phenyl via conjugated double bond, and methyl ester. Might match the template: the product side includes a phenylpropyl chain attached to carbonyl, but our target has phenyl attached via double bond to carbonyl carbon? Actually target: carbonyl carbon attached to C1 which is part of cyclobutene with silyl substituent, and also double bond to phenyl via /C=C/. So maybe the template matches.

We need to apply template to target to get precursors. Use apply_template tool.
